what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted by roll call to waive the annual grease trap fee again this year, with a letter to customers saying compliance is still expected.
The waiver covers 18 customers, and the sewer budget is absorbing the lost fee revenue.
Staff are drafting proposals for the town's expected federal ARPA payments, such as a pump station evaluation and upgrade, to go on the next agenda.
The manager reported that the Fitchburg sewer invoice reflected a rate increase and was in the budget, and that FY21 revenues exceeded expenses.
A direct mailing to unconnected properties along sewer lines was planned, and the next meetings were set for August 10 and August 31.

why_it_matters: Sewer users, not the general tax levy, carry the cost of the waived grease trap fee, so it affects the revenue that sets sewer rates.
ARPA money for sewer projects such as a pump station could reduce what ratepayers would otherwise have to fund, and the proposals will be set out on the next agenda.
watch_next: ARPA proposals on the next meeting agenda; the next meetings are August 10 (remote) and August 31 (in person at town hall).
